## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## User Instructions

</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>"
  }
}

commands.description: (bio-research) Deep learning for single-cell analysis using scvi-tools. This skill should be used when users need (1) data integration and batch correction with scVI/scANVI, (2) ATAC-seq analysis with PeakVI, (3) CITE-seq multi-modal analysis with totalVI, (4) multiome RNA+ATAC analysis with MultiVI, (5) spatial transcriptomics deconvolution with DestVI, (6) label transfer and reference mapping with scANVI/scArches, (7) RNA velocity with veloVI, or (8) any deep learning-based single-cell method. Triggers include mentions of scVI, scANVI, totalVI, PeakVI, MultiVI, DestVI, veloVI, sysVI, scArches, variational autoencoder, VAE, batch correction, data integration, multi-modal, CITE-seq, multiome, reference mapping, latent space.

commands.name: bio-research:single-cell-rna-qc
commands.description: (bio-research) Performs quality control on single-cell RNA-seq data (.h5ad or .h5 files) using scverse best practices with MAD-based filtering and comprehensive visualizations. Use when users request QC analysis, filtering low-quality cells, assessing data quality, or following scverse/scanpy best practices for single-cell analysis.

commands.name: cowork-plugin-management:cowork-plugin-customizer
commands.description: (cowork-plugin-management) Customize or personalize a Claude Code plugin for a specific organization's tools and workflows. Use when users want to customize a plugin, replace tool placeholders, or configure MCP servers for a plugin. This skill requires Cowork mode with mounted plugin directories and will not work in remote or standard CLI sessions.

commands.name: kdbx-knowledge:kdbx
commands.description: (kdbx-knowledge) Use when working with KDB-X modules, AI libraries (vector search, HNSW, IVF, BM25, time-series similarity, anomaly detection), GPU acceleration, Parquet, kURL REST client, object storage, or the module framework. Also use when encountering module-not-found errors, vector dimension mismatches, HNSW index issues, GPU setup issues, or `nyi` errors from using `\l` instead of `use`.

commands.name: kdbx-knowledge:kdbx-db-service
commands.description: (kdbx-knowledge) Use this skill whenever working with the KDB-X DB Service - a containerised time-series database distributed via Docker Compose. Trigger for any task involving: setting up or resetting the DB Service, ingesting data (CSV, streaming, REST, or third-party sources like OneTick), writing or optimising queries (Python client, q client, or REST/qSQL), or planning an end-to-end ingest pipeline. Also trigger for schema design questions, troubleshooting ingest jobs, or any reference to `dbservice_client`, `session.import_files`, `session.import_data`, `session.query_simple`, `session.query_sql`, `session.query_q`, `session.querySimple`, `session.querySQL`, `session.queryQ`, or the DB Service REST API on port 8080. Also trigger for: "run the FX recipe", "FX ingest recipe", "run the OneTick recipe", "run the OneTick LSE recipe", "run the OneTick LSE runbook", or any request to set up the full OneTick batch pipeline end-to-end from download through to ingest. Do NOT trigger for: KX Dashboards configuration; generic Docker Compose questions unrelated to the DB Service stack; or plain kdb+/q questions that don't reference the DB Service.

commands.name: kdbx-knowledge:kxmeta-author
commands.description: (kdbx-knowledge) Writing qdoc annotations for `aimeta` so the compiler publishes tables and functions correctly. Mandatory `@kind`/`@name` markers, the chained `@col` modifier form, q-language traps that silently drop items, and the recompile loop. Use when adding or editing `/ @kind ...` annotation blocks in a q codebase that loads `aimeta`, or when annotated items aren't surfacing in `meta.json`. For the wire model & tag vocabulary see ../../reference/agent-guide.md.

commands.name: kdbx-knowledge:kxmeta-discover
commands.description: (kdbx-knowledge) Discovering metadata on a running kdb+ process via `aimeta` — cold-start probing, the `/meta` HTTP route, `kx-meta discover`, qIPC fallback, and reading the `tier` / `references[]` fields in the response. Use when an agent needs to learn what tables and functions a kdb+ host exposes, when interpreting `kx-meta discover` output, when handling tier-1 fallback gracefully, or when walking `references[]` for vocabulary resolution. For the wire model and full `meta.json` shape see ../../reference/agent-guide.md.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-accordion
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants collapsible or expandable sections in a KX Dashboards layout. Use it for section-based content organization; use kx-tabs for tabbed switching and kx-flex-panel for non-collapsible flexible layout containers.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-actions
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this alongside a component skill when adding KX Dashboards interactions such as clicks, hovers, row selection, navigation, or data-source re-execution. It defines how actions are attached and triggered, not the base component itself.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-basiccomponents-containers
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this for KX Dashboards layout containers and navigation primitives such as panels, navigation menus, and overlay drawers. Use it for structural layout needs; use kx-tabs for tabbed switching, kx-accordion for collapsible sections, and kx-flex-panel for fixed-plus-flex layouts.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-breadcrumbs
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards breadcrumb trail for hierarchical drilldown or drill-through navigation, especially with pivot grids or chart-based exploration. Use kx-tabs for tabbed navigation instead of breadcrumbs.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-button
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards button or clickable action trigger: labels, icons, tooltips, alignment, fixed width, disabled state, colours, and click actions. Use it for buttons and action triggers; use kx-textinput for free-text entry, kx-dropdown for selection lists, or kx-selectioncontrols for radio/checkbox choices.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-chart3d
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards 3D chart or 3D visualisation: scatter, line, bar, surface, or 4D color/size-encoded layers. Use it for 3D graphics; use kx-chartgl for standard 2D WebGL charts and kx-gauge for dial or bullet-style KPI charts.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-chartgl
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards ChartGL chart or chart layer: line, bar, bubble, waterfall, candlestick, multi-axis, streaming, or other WebGL-accelerated visualisations. Use kx-heatmap for standalone heatmap components; read kx-dashboard-core first for the dashboard envelope, data sources, ViewState, and checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-dashboard-core
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when building or editing any KX Dashboards JSON dashboard: start here for the dashboard envelope, screens, widget wrapper, ViewState, data sources, actions, notifications, deployment, and the pre-flight checklist. Load it before component skills such as kx-chartgl, kx-datagrid, kx-pivot-grid, or kx-query when you are assembling a full dashboard or wiring its shared infrastructure.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-datafilter
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Generate KX Dashboards input and filter components: DataFilter (visual filter builder, definitionId=48) and QueryBuilder (visual kdb+ query constructor, definitionId=10254). Use when the user asks for a filter panel, filter builder, AND/OR filter, or query builder for a grid or chart. Critical: DataFilter requires a two-data-source + ViewState bridge — always follow that pattern. For parameter input forms and Dataform (definitionId=27) use the kx-dataform skill instead. Not for a simple single/multi value picker bound to a ViewState (use kx-dropdown or kx-selectioncontrols). Also read kx-dashboard-core for envelope, data sources, ViewState, and the agent checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-dataform
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards parameter-input form that writes values into ViewStates and re-executes a data source on submit: simple input panels, forms with dropdowns, date pickers, sliders, or password fields. Use kx-formbuilder for free-form record entry and kx-datafilter for filter/query-builder UIs instead.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-datagrid
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a flat, row-by-row KX Dashboards table for browsing or editing records (trade blotter, price table, real-time table, sortable grid, editable grid). Do not use it for aggregated pivot-style analysis; use kx-pivot-grid for that. Read kx-dashboard-core first for the shared dashboard envelope, data sources, ViewState, and checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-datepicker
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards date or time picker: calendar date, datetime, timestamp, timespan, or month input bound to a ViewState. The picker mode is determined by the ViewState type bound to SelectedDate. Also read kx-dashboard-core for envelope, data sources, ViewState, and the agent checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-dropdown
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards dropdown or multi-select list for picking one or more values: symbol selectors, filter lists, dependent dropdowns, grouped items, or static option lists. Use kx-selectioncontrols for radio buttons or checkboxes and kx-datafilter for multi-condition filter-builder UIs.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-flex-panel
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when a KX Dashboards layout needs a fixed header, footer, or sidebar beside a flexible main content area. Use it for pinned-plus-fill layouts; use kx-basiccomponents-containers for general panels and drawers and kx-tabs for tabbed switching.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-formbuilder
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards data-entry form that collects user values for submission or editing, including dynamic forms, validators, and form-state output to ViewStates. Use kx-dataform for parameter-input forms that re-run data sources on submit rather than general data entry.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-gauge
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards gauge, dial, speedometer, or bullet-style KPI visual. Use it for progress and target-vs-actual displays; use kx-chartgl for conventional charts and kx-pie for proportional segment charts.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-handlebars
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when a KX Dashboards component needs Handlebars templating for labels, tooltips, KPI text, or other dynamic content. Read it when generating or debugging Template, CustomTooltip, TooltipTemplate, or advancedTooltip fields.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-heatmap
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Generate KX Dashboards Heatmap/Treemap component: hierarchical treemap visualisation (key=Heatmap, componentName=Treemap, definitionId=5). Use for: treemap, heatmap, treechart, market map, portfolio map, proportional area chart, group-by hierarchy, colour-coded tiles, node size/colour. Data[] layers define display column, size column, colour column, and highlight rules. ColorPalette drives tile colouring. GroupBy creates nested parent/child hierarchy. Not for a heatmap layer on an X/Y chart (use kx-chartgl's Heatmap layer) or a geographic heatmap on map tiles (use kx-offline-map); this is a standalone hierarchical treemap/heatmap of coloured tiles. Also read kx-dashboard-core for envelope, data sources, ViewState, and the agent checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-maps
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this only when the user explicitly wants a KX Dashboards Google Maps GeoMap. For standard offline or custom tile-server maps, use kx-offline-map or kx-quad-map instead.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-offline-map
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Generate KX Dashboards OfflineMap components (MapLibre/MapTiler, definitionId=1035). ⭐ DEFAULT map type — use this whenever the user asks for a map, geographic visualization, points on a map, heatmap, animated circles, GeoJSON overlay, offline map, or tile map in a KX Dashboard, UNLESS the user explicitly requests Google Maps (use kx-maps GeoMap). Covers all sub-sections: Points, Circles, Lines, Heatmap, HeatmapGrid, AnimatedCircles, ConcentricCircles, Layers, Annotation, Bounds, Icons, NightDayLayer, TileServer, ExternalAPI, Export, and Interactions. For WMTS / OpenLayers custom tile-server maps use kx-quad-map instead.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-pie
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Generate a KX Dashboards PieJS component: pie or donut chart of proportional segments (key=PieJS, definitionId=1009). Use for: pie chart, donut chart, doughnut, share-of-total, proportional segments, percentage breakdown, part-to-whole, categorical composition, market share, portfolio allocation. DataSet.Label is the categorical column and DataSet.Layers[n].Segment is the numeric value column; DonutRatio > 0 makes it a donut. Use kx-chartgl for line/bar/area charts and kx-gauge for KPI-style gauges. Also read kx-dashboard-core for envelope, data sources, ViewState, and the agent checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-pivot-grid
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards Pivot Grid or pivot-table-style experience: aggregated drilldown grids, breakdown/aggregate views, OLAP-style analysis, or a grid linked to Breadcrumbs. It is the right choice for pivot-style analysis; use kx-datagrid for flat, record-level tables instead. Load kx-dashboard-core first.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-playback
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Generate KX Dashboards PlayBack component: time-series playback controller (definitionId=47, key=PlayBack). Use for: playback, time-series replay, animate data, step through events, timeline scrubber, playback speed control, data animation. Mode=Event steps through data rows; Mode=Time uses a time column. Selected ViewState receives the current position. Also read kx-dashboard-core for envelope, data sources, ViewState, and the agent checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-quad-map
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Generate KX Dashboards QuadMap components (OpenLayers/WMTS, definitionId=1036). Use QuadMap when the user asks for a tile-server map, WMTS map, or OpenLayers map. QuadMap supports Circle/Icon/Line data layers and annotation drawing, but for a standard point/line map without a custom tile server prefer kx-offline-map. For requests involving Google Maps use kx-maps GeoMap; for MapLibre/MapTiler use kx-offline-map. Also read kx-dashboard-core for envelope, data sources, ViewState, and the agent checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-query
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when creating or changing a KX Dashboards data source: choose the data type, write or validate a kdb+/SQL query, wire ViewState parameters, set polling or streaming, or bind query results to widgets. Read it before generating queries for charts, grids, forms, maps, or actions in a dashboard.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-radar
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards radar or polar-area chart for comparing dimensions or categories. Use it for radial comparison visuals; use kx-chartgl for standard chart types such as line, bar, or candlestick.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-selectioncontrols
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants simple KX Dashboards radio buttons or checkboxes for a single or multiple selection choice. Use kx-dropdown for searchable or dependent selection lists and kx-datafilter for multi-condition filter-builder panels.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-specialist
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Generate KX Dashboards specialist and visualisation components: EditableList (watchlist, definitionId=668), TreeView (hierarchical tree, definitionId=2002), Trade (Level 2 order book, definitionId=1013), ActionTracker (alert workflow, definitionId=1001), Bitmap (EmbedPy/matplotlib image, definitionId=1999), Graph (force-directed/network graph, definitionId=11110). Triggers: watchlist, editable list, tree, hierarchy, order book, trade book, alert tracker, matplotlib image, network graph, force directed. For PieJS (definitionId=1009) use kx-pie. For Gauge (definitionId=11178) use kx-gauge. For Heatmap (definitionId=5) use kx-heatmap. For PlayBack (definitionId=47) use kx-playback. For Radar (definitionId=1008) use kx-radar. For Breadcrumbs (definitionId=19) use kx-breadcrumbs. Also read kx-dashboard-core for envelope, data sources, ViewState, and the agent checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-tabs
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards tabbed interface that switches between grouped content sections. Use it for tabbed navigation or content organization; use kx-accordion for collapsible sections and kx-basiccomponents-containers for general panels and drawers.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-text
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Generate KX Dashboards text display component: Text (static or dynamic label/heading/paragraph/KPI tile, definitionId=17). Use for: label, heading, title, paragraph, static text, rich text, HTML markup, dynamic text from a data source, ViewState-interpolated text via Handlebars template, single-value scalar display, KPI tile, metric card, stat display, total count, aggregate result. IMPORTANT: when a query returns a single value (count, sum, last price, etc.), always use Text — never Dropdown. ComponentName=Text, key=BasicComponents. Also read kx-dashboard-core for envelope, data sources, ViewState, and the agent checklist.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-textinput
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Use this when the user wants a KX Dashboards free-text input box: search boxes, filter inputs, symbol entry, or multiline text entry. Use kx-button for clickable triggers, kx-datepicker for calendar selection, and kx-selectioncontrols for radio buttons or checkboxes.

commands.name: kx-dashboards-knowledge:kx-texttospeech
commands.description: (kx-dashboards-knowledge) Generate KX Dashboards TextToSpeech component: text display with browser speech synthesis (definitionId=36, ComponentName=TextToSpeech, key=BasicComponents). Use for: text to speech, read aloud, voice output, speech synthesis, audio narration, spoken data. Shares HtmlText/Template/Data pattern with the Text component. SpeechOptions controls Voice, Rate, CacheData, and ShowPlayPause. Also read kx-dashboard-core for envelope, data sources, ViewState, and the agent checklist.

commands.name: onetick-knowledge:onetick-cloud
commands.description: (onetick-knowledge) Compose and execute OneTick SQL against KX OneTick Cloud. Use when the user asks to query OneTick, retrieve tick / bar / daily / order-book / reference data, run a SQL statement against a OneTick database (e.g. LSE_SAMPLE, US_COMP_SAMPLE, LSE_SAMPLE_BARS, US_COMP_SAMPLE_DAILY, OTQ_CHAIN), pull market data from OneTick Cloud, convert a natural-language data request into a OneTick SQL query plus its result set, explain how the OneTick execution helper / auth / onetick-py WebAPI wheel works, describe how the helper handles large results, previews, or errors, or show an `onetick-py` / `otp.DataSource` Python idiom for OneTick data access.

commands.name: pykx-knowledge:pykx
commands.description: (pykx-knowledge) Use when working with KDB-X Python for Python-to-q data conversion, querying tables with Column API, IPC connections, DB management, or integrating Python with q. Also use when encountering type conversion issues, connection errors, or licensed vs unlicensed mode questions.

commands.name: q-knowledge:q
commands.description: (q-knowledge) Use when writing, editing, reviewing, or debugging q/kdb+ code (.q files), querying kdb+ tables, translating Python to q, running q from shell, doing time-series analysis, or optimizing q performance. Also use when encountering q errors ('assign, 'rank, 'type), reserved-word conflicts, right-to-left evaluation bugs, or atom/vector type mismatches. Trigger whenever the user is working with .q files, kdb+ tables, or qsql queries even if they don't explicitly ask for q help.

commands.name: q-knowledge:qlint-snippet
commands.description: (q-knowledge) Lint a single q/qSQL code snippet using KX qlint. Reads code from stdin or argument and prints the raw lint table. Use when the user says "qlint this snippet", "lint this q code", "check syntax of <code>", "qlint snippet", or wants quick lint feedback on a piece of q code. Also trigger whenever Claude has just generated q code and should validate it before presenting to the user.

commands.name: frontend-design:frontend-design
commands.description: (frontend-design) Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.

commands.name: superpowers:brainstorming
commands.description: (superpowers) You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation).

commands.name: superpowers:diagnosing-superpowers
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when a superpowers session went wrong and your human partner wants to know why — repeated work, ignored plans, stumbles, poor results, a skill that didn't fire, "it took too long", "why is it so expensive", "what is it doing" — or wants to build a bug report for the superpowers maintainers, for the current session or a past one identified by id or path, on any harness.

commands.name: superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies

commands.name: superpowers:executing-plans
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when executing an implementation plan in the current session as the implementer yourself — your human partner chose inline execution, or no subagent tool is available

commands.name: superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work

commands.name: superpowers:receiving-code-review
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation

commands.name: superpowers:requesting-code-review
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements

commands.name: superpowers:subagent-driven-development
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session

commands.name: superpowers:systematic-debugging
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes

commands.name: superpowers:test-driven-development
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

commands.name: superpowers:using-git-worktrees
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback

commands.name: superpowers:using-superpowers
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions

commands.name: superpowers:verification-before-completion
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

commands.name: superpowers:writing-plans
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code

commands.name: superpowers:writing-skills
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment

commands.name: skill-creator:skill-creator
commands.description: (skill-creator) Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

commands.name: duckdb-skills:attach-db
commands.description: (duckdb-skills) Attach a DuckDB database file for use with /duckdb-skills:query. Explores the schema (tables, columns, row counts) and writes a SQL state file so subsequent queries can restore this session automatically via duckdb -init.

commands.name: duckdb-skills:convert-file
commands.description: (duckdb-skills) Convert any data file to another format: CSV, Parquet, JSON, Excel, GeoJSON, and more. Use when the user says "convert to parquet", "save as xlsx", "export as JSON", "make this a CSV", "turn into parquet", or any variation of format-to-format conversion for data files. Also triggers when the user wants to write Parquet, Excel, or other binary formats that Claude cannot produce natively.

commands.name: duckdb-skills:duckdb-docs
commands.description: (duckdb-skills) Search DuckDB and DuckLake documentation and blog posts. Returns relevant doc chunks for a question or keyword using full-text search against a locally cached index.

commands.name: duckdb-skills:install-duckdb
commands.description: (duckdb-skills) Install or update DuckDB extensions. Each argument is either a plain extension name (installs from core) or name@repo (e.g. magic@community). Pass --update to update extensions instead of installing.

commands.name: duckdb-skills:query
commands.description: (duckdb-skills) Run SQL queries against the attached DuckDB database or ad-hoc against files. Accepts raw SQL or natural language questions. Uses DuckDB Friendly SQL idioms.

commands.name: duckdb-skills:read-file
commands.description: (duckdb-skills) Read any data file (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro, Excel, spatial, SQLite) or remote URL (S3, HTTPS). Use when user references a data file, asks "what's in this file", or wants to preview/profile a dataset. Not for source code.

commands.name: duckdb-skills:read-memories
commands.description: (duckdb-skills) Search past Claude Code session logs to recall prior decisions, patterns, or unresolved work. Use when user says "do you remember", "what did we do", references past conversations, or you need context from prior sessions.

commands.name: duckdb-skills:s3-explore
commands.description: (duckdb-skills) Explore and query data on S3, Cloudflare R2, GCS, MinIO, or any S3-compatible storage. Use when the user mentions an s3://, r2://, gs://, or gcs:// URL, asks "what's in this bucket", wants to list remote files, preview remote Parquet/CSV/JSON, or query data on object storage without downloading it. Also triggers when the user wants to know the size, schema, or row count of remote datasets.

commands.name: duckdb-skills:spatial
commands.description: (duckdb-skills) Answer questions about spatial data using DuckDB. Use when the user mentions locations, coordinates, lat/lng, distances, maps, addresses, "near", "within", "closest", geographic names, or spatial file formats (GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage, GPX, GeoParquet). Also triggers when the user wants to find places, buildings, or roads — Overture Maps provides free global data on S3 with zero API keys. Handles spatial joins, distance calculations, containment checks, density analysis, and format conversions for geographic data.

commands.name: runpod:companion-clis
commands.description: (Runpod) Companion CLIs for Runpod workflows — HuggingFace, GitHub, Docker, and AWS. Use the ComfyUI model-repair guide in runpod-templates instead when an imported ComfyUI workflow lacks model download metadata.

commands.name: runpod:flash
commands.description: (Runpod) runpod-flash — code-first serverless: write Python locally, run it on remote Runpod GPUs/CPUs with `flash dev` (hot-reload + live worker logs), then `flash deploy`. Use for @Endpoint/@remote functions, resource config, and debugging flash deployments. For CLI-only infra management use runpodctl or runpod-mcp.

commands.name: runpod:runpod
commands.description: (Runpod) Start here for any Runpod task — running GPU/CPU pods, deploying serverless endpoints, templates, network volumes, building images, or understanding how Runpod works. Routes to the right skill (runpod-mcp, runpodctl, flash, companion-clis, runpod-usage, runpod-templates, runpod-migrate) and indexes two dozen live-verified end-to-end examples (golden paths) — use it when the lane is unclear, and for any multi-step or provisioning task even when it is not.

commands.name: runpod:runpod-mcp
commands.description: (Runpod) Manage Runpod infrastructure — pods, serverless endpoints, jobs, templates, network volumes, container-registry auth, GPU/CPU catalog, and billing — via the Runpod MCP server's structured tool calls. Use when the Runpod MCP tools (create-pod, list-endpoints, …) are connected in this session, or to connect them (hosted OAuth or local npx). Prefer this over runpodctl for plain infra CRUD when MCP is available; use runpodctl for the terminal, file transfer, or SSH setup.

commands.name: runpod:runpod-migrate
commands.description: (Runpod) Migrate a codebase from the Runpod GraphQL API or REST v1 to REST v2 — inventory which parts use which API version, rewrite the call sites, flag breaking changes, and verify. Use when someone asks to move to v2, asks what v2 would change, or asks which Runpod API their code is on. For managing infrastructure rather than migrating code, use runpod-mcp or runpodctl.

commands.name: runpod:runpod-templates
commands.description: (Runpod) Runpod's official prebuilt pod templates (ComfyUI, PyTorch, and others): what each image ships, which ports and paths it uses, how to pick one, how to pin a version, and what is missing on first boot. Use when a task says "run <X> on a pod" and an official template already covers it, instead of building an image — and when a user needs help with or wants to fix something about a Runpod template they are already running (won't boot, can't reach the UI, missing models, wrong CUDA line, broken ComfyUI workflow metadata on imported workflows): start here and route onward. Deploy with runpodctl or runpod-mcp; end-to-end walkthroughs live in the runpod router's golden paths.

commands.name: runpod:runpod-usage
commands.description: (Runpod) How Runpod works and how to work it — pods vs serverless, GPU/VRAM selection, storage, building a container, networking, plus the agentic pod development loop (provision → ssh-exec → set up → poll readiness) and on-pod install hygiene (uv/apt). Use to answer "how does X work", "which GPU", "how do I build a container", or "how do I stand up a workload on a pod". Guidance, not a tool — execute with runpodctl, runpod-mcp, or flash.

commands.name: runpod:runpodctl
commands.description: (Runpod) Runpod CLI for managing GPU/CPU workloads from the terminal — pods, serverless endpoints, templates, network volumes, Hub deploys, models, SSH, and file transfer (send/receive). Use for terminal/CI/scripting, Hub browse/deploy, SSH setup, `doctor`, or when the Runpod MCP tools are not connected. For structured tool calls in an MCP-enabled session, prefer runpod-mcp.

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". commands.name: verify

Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

  "summary": "I'm approving the Phase 4 plan. It meets all six criteria, and nothing in it would fail the exit check or break a CLAUDE.md rule.\n\n(1) **Task coverage.** Every task in the phase block is covered.\n- `dtw_rerank.py`: anchored segments, banded `dtw_ndim` with `use_c=True` and `require_c()`, \u00a79.3 normalization, \u03c4 calibration and warp ratio.\n- The optional LB_Keogh pruning is left out on purpose, with a reason (A2).\n- `fusion.py`: the seven \u00a710.5 features and a frozen `FusionModel`. Training pairs are built in `eval/training.py`. Both `models/fusion_v1.json` and `models/dtw_calibration.json` are written.\n- `explain.py`, `matcher.py`, a real `make models`, and `match --method dtw`.\n\n(2) **Tests.** Each test bullet has a named test:\n- self-distance \u2248 0: `test_self_distance_is_zero`;\n- warped copy scores high and reports its warp: `test_time_warped_copy_scores_high_and_reports_its_warp`, warps 0.8 to 1.4 with a \u00b10.03 tolerance;\n- copycat fuses lower than P1: `test_copycat_fuses_lower_than_true_p1`, plus the slow full-data test `test_full_copycat_fuses_lower_than_p1`;\n- model round trip: `test_model_round_trip`;\n- determinism: `test_dtw_matcher_is_deterministic`, `test_training_is_deterministic` and the slow `test_full_models_are_deterministic`.\n\n(3) **Exit check.** Each criterion maps to a command and the evidence it produces: `make models`, `make eval` (the `recall_at_5_t120`, `dtw_lift`, `copycat_first_t120` and latency keys, and the demo rows), `match --at 90`, `eval --baseline` and `check_targets.py 4`. The plan also covers the case where `make eval` exits 1 and the `&&` chain stops. I checked the code:\n- `check_targets.py` names exactly the keys the plan adds, and requires `method != euclidean` and `reports/baseline.json`.\n- `eval --baseline` writes the file and exits 0.\n- `reports/` and `models/` are not gitignored.\n- scikit-learn is already a dependency, and the dtaidistance C path loads (`try_import_c()` returns True).\n\n(4) **Rules.**\n- Truth: only `eval/training.py` reads truth, and the source scan covers the new modules.\n- No look-ahead: the `start < q.start` filter is kept, the own incident is excluded, a DTW no-look-ahead test is added, and the partial live signature uses RF, Remote ID and concurrency data only up to T, with a tamper test.\n- Determinism: rows are sorted before an lbfgs fit, there are no random draws, and a training hash is recorded.\n- Ports: two read-only port methods are added through the DuckDB adapter and logged as D-072.\n- Tests: two stub assertions are replaced by stronger ones and none are skipped. No \u00a719 target is lowered; DTW latency is measured on 500 candidates, which is harder than \u00a710.9's 50.\n\n(5) **Documentation.** The plan lists EXIT_CHECK.md, REPORT.md, the `match`, `eval`, `features`, `store`, `config` and root package READMEs, the root README Status, PROGRESS.md (session log and one-line evidence, leaving the Status cell alone) and D-068 to D-077.\n\n(6) **No human decision needed.** D-062 is already resolved by D-064, and the D-058 fix (fixed-unit prefilter vectors, 500 candidates) leaves the demo story unchanged.\n\nThe main risk is research, not process. In the planning prototype CHARLIE-260710 was third and ALPHA-0502 fourth, so the live top 3 may miss by one place. The plan has honest mitigations: settings are chosen on the training split only, nothing is special-cased for the demo, and a miss is recorded as a soft gap under D-063.",

First, if a `baseline.json` from the Euclidean run is in the same reports folder: DTW end-to-end latency is well above 1.5 \u00d7 the Euclidean baseline + 2 ms, which counts as a regression. 1	# Phase 4: DTW matcher and fusion model, plan
2	
3	Autopilot plan step, 2026-10-28. Written without a human in the loop (CLAUDE.md rule 5, `phase-auto`):
4	every assumption below is recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` during the build.
5	
6	## Goal
7	
8	Build the real matcher (SPEC §10.4 to §10.8): a DTW re-rank of the prefilter's candidates, a calibrated
9	shape similarity, a logistic fusion of shape and context features trained on history only, warp ratio,
10	explanations, `make models`, and `kairos-defense match --method dtw`. Then run `make eval` with the DTW
11	matcher and write the first `reports/baseline.json`.
12	
13	Phase 4 targets (SPEC §20, `scripts/check_targets.py 4`): Recall@5 at T = 120 s ≥ 0.80, DTW lift ≥ +0.10,
14	copycat-first ≤ 5%, the §10.9 latencies (report only, D-060), and the demo rows
15	`live_first_contact_local`, `live_orbit_established_s` and `live_top3_incidents`, all `pass`. At T+90 the
16	live top 3 must be P1-DELTA-260419, P1-ALPHA-260303 and P1-ALPHA-260502 (any order), each with a score
17	and reasons.
18	
19	## Inputs read
20	
21	- `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/PROGRESS.md` (phases 0 to 3 and their backfills), `docs/phases/TEMPLATES.md`,
22	  `docs/phases/phase-03/REPORT.md`, `docs/phases/gates.json`, `scripts/check_targets.py`.
23	- SPEC §1.2 (T+90 beat: "flown ~18% slower"), §6.5, §7.2, §7.5, §8.10, §9 (§9.3's normalization), §10
24	  (all), §19 (all), §20 phase 4.
25	- `docs/DECISIONS.md`, in particular D-003, D-013, D-020, D-046, D-047, D-048, D-049, D-050, D-051,
26	  D-053 to D-060, D-062 to D-064 and D-067. Next free number: **D-068**.
27	- Code: `match/` (query, prefilter, baseline, types), `features/windows.py`, `features/channels.py`,
28	  `features/signatures.py`, `store/duck.py`, `store/lance.py`, `ports.py`, `config/scoring.py`,
29	  `eval/` (harness, metrics, demo, report, truth), `cli.py`, and the tests that touch them
30	  (`test_cli.py`, `test_eval_harness.py`, `test_no_lookahead.py`, `test_windows.py`,
31	  `test_truth_isolation.py`, `tests/slow/test_full_index.py`).
32	
33	### Facts checked during planning (read-only; nothing in the repo or `data/` was written)
34	
35	1. **The C path works on the laptop (D-062 resolved by D-064).** `dtw.try_import_c()` is True.
36	   `dtw_ndim.distance(L, S, window=60, use_c=True)` on 120×5 against 240×5 takes 0.064 ms.
37	   `dtw_ndim.warping_paths(..., use_c=True)` (or `warping_paths_fast`) plus `dtw.best_path` takes
38	   0.4 ms. Without `use_c` it takes 36 ms, so every call must pass `use_c=True`.
39	2. **LanceDB returns many candidate tracks cheaply.** For the live query at T+90 (W = 60, filtered),
40	   `k` = 200 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 windows gives 185 / 1,102 / 1,545 / 1,728 distinct tracks in about
41	   14 / 18 / 21 / 25 ms. Loading all 800,148 `track_features` rows takes 46 ms (58 MB). 50 separate
42	   `features()` calls take 76 ms.
43	3. **D-058's cause is the per-window z-normalization, and option (a) fixes most of it.** A brute-force
44	   rebuild of the 60 s and 120 s windows in memory with fixed per-channel scales (speed 5 m/s, turn
45	   10 °/s, distance 200 m, altitude 30 m, climb 1 m/s; times the §6.5 weights; then PAA and L2) instead
46	   of per-window z-normalization gives:
47	
48	   | Same-actor track among the candidates (23 prober queries) | per-window z (phase 3) | fixed scales |
49	   |---|---:|---:|
50	   | top 50 at T = 90 s | 0.70 | 0.91 |
51	   | top 50 at T = 120 s | 0.74 | 0.83 |
52	   | top 200 at T = 120 s | 0.78 | 0.96 |
53	   | live T+90: ranks of DELTA, ALPHA-0303, ALPHA-0502 among 1,882 tracks | 855 / 953 / 564 | 318 / 23 / 436 |
54	
55	4. **The full pipeline, prototyped, reaches the targets with a wide candidate list (D-058 (a) + (b)).**
56	   This was a scratch prototype: §10.4 anchored segments with per-series z-normalized banded DTW, the
57	   seven §10.5 features, τ = median same-actor `d_norm`, and `LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced")`
58	   trained on months 1 to 12 (54 prober and copycat queries at T = 60, 90, 120). It was evaluated on the
59	   23 month 13 to 18 prober queries.
60	
61	   | Prefilter vectors, candidates | Recall@5 T=120 | top 3 T=90 | copycat-first T=120 | Euclidean Recall@5 T=120 | live T+90 ranks DELTA / ALPHA-0303 / ALPHA-0502 |
62	   |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
63	   | fixed, 50 | 0.83 | 0.91 | 0.13 | 0.43 | – / 1 / – |
64	   | fixed, 200 | 0.96 | 0.96 | 0.00 | 0.43 | – / 1 / – |
65	   | **fixed, 500** | **1.00** | **0.96** | **0.00** | **0.43** | **1 / 2 / 4** (CHARLIE 3rd) |
66	   | per-window z, 500 | 0.91 | 0.91 | 0.09 | 0.48 | – / – / – |
67	   | dataset σ (global z), 500 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.00 | 0.61 | 2 / 3 / 5 (BRAVO-251114 1st, CHARLIE 4th) |
68	   | fixed, 500, DTW on fixed scales too | 1.00 | 0.96 | 0.00 | 0.43 | 4 / 1 / 20 |
69	   | fixed, 500, extra `target_match` feature | 1.00 | 0.96 | 0.00 | 0.43 | 5 / 17 / 20 |
70	
71	   With the best setting the live top 3 misses by one place: CHARLIE-260710, the planted "weaker match
72	   on purpose", is third, and ALPHA-0502 is fourth. Both are true P1 flights. **Disclosure:** these
73	   planning numbers looked at the month 13 to 18 queries and the demo. The build chooses its settings
74	   by the training-split rule in "Assumptions" A3, not by these tables.
75	5. **§10.4's warp ratio cannot work as literally written.** Aligning a W-row live matrix end to end
76	   with a 2W-row anchored segment forces the path slope to about 1.7 whatever the true warp: a synthetic
77	   flight warped by 1.0 / 1.22 / 0.95 / 0.8 gives slopes 1.67 / 1.74 / 1.65 / 1.63. Normalizing each
78	   series over itself also biases it, even with relaxed ends: 1.38 / 1.58 / 1.31 / 1.06. With **both**
79	   series normalized by the live window's μ and σ **and** psi relaxation on the segment's two ends
80	   (`psi = (0, 0, m − n, m − n)`, best end column of the last row, `dtw.best_path(paths, row=n, col=j)`),
81	   the slopes are 1.002 / 1.221 / 0.95 / 0.80 / 1.40 for W = 60 and W = 120. A warp of 1.22 then gives
82	   "18% slower", which is the §1.2 beat.
83	
84	## Assumptions and decisions
85	
86	Each one becomes a `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry during the build (numbers are provisional).
87	
88	- **A1 · D-068 · D-058 resolved: fixed-unit window vectors plus a wide candidate list.**
89	  - `features.channel_scales: [5.0, 10.0, 200.0, 30.0, 1.0]` (m/s, °/s, m, m, m/s) and
90	    `windows.normalize: fixed` are new keys in `config/scoring.yaml`. `fixed` means
91	    `raw / scale × weight`, with no centering, the D-051 NaN interpolation, then PAA and L2. `window`
92	    keeps phase 3's per-window z-normalization (§9.3 as written) for comparison and for the phase 3
93	    unit tests.
94	  - `prefilter.k_windows: 10000` and `prefilter.candidate_tracks: 500`.
95	  - This deviates from §9.3 (normalization "over the series being compared") for the prefilter vectors
96	    only; DTW keeps §9.3 (A2). It also deviates from §6.5's 200 / 50.
97	  - Why: fact 3 and fact 4. Per-window z-normalization erases the orbit radius, the speeds and the
98	    altitude that make P1 distinctive. The DTW plus fusion cost of 500 candidates is about 30 ms.
99	  - `make index` must be rerun. A self-check refuses a stale index (A8).
100	- **A2 · D-069 · DTW details (§10.4).**
101	  - Shape distance as written: anchored segment `[o − 0.5W, o + 1.5W]` clipped to the track; each series
102	    z-normalized over itself and weighted (§9.3); NaN interpolated, an all-NaN channel set to 0;
103	    `dtw_ndim.distance(L, S, window=int(0.25 × max(n, m)), use_c=True)`;
104	    `d_norm = d / sqrt(n)`; `shape_sim = exp(−d_norm / τ)`.
105	  - The C path is mandatory (D-013, D-020): `require_c()` raises `DtwUnavailable` when
106	    `dtw.try_import_c()` is False. Every call passes `use_c=True`.
107	  - Warp ratio (fact 5): a second alignment with L and S both scaled by L's μ and σ (weighted), psi
108	    relaxation `(0, 0, m − n, m − n)` when `m > n` (none otherwise), and the same band. Take the best
109	    end column of the last row, then `dtw.best_path`. `k` is the least-squares slope of segment index
110	    against live index. It is computed for the top `EXPLAIN_TOP = 20` fused matches only (the ones shown
111	    and explained); the others keep `warp_ratio = NaN` (no invented numbers, D-054).
112	  - Text (§10.4 step 5): `k > 1.1` → "flown X% slower" with X = round((1 − 1/k) × 100); `k < 0.9` →
113	    "flown X% faster" with X = round((1/k − 1) × 100). §10.4 gives only the slower formula; the faster one
114	    is its mirror.
115	  - Step 6: `explain_alignment()` wraps `subsequence_alignment` on the `dist_target_m` channel and is
116	    tested now. The phase 8 Match Explainer will call it.
117	  - The optional LB_Keogh pruning is not built: 500 DTW calls take about 30 ms, and `lb_keogh` needs
118	    equal lengths while L and S differ.
119	- **A3 · D-070 · Settings are chosen on the training split only.** If the build needs to choose among
120	  pre-registered alternatives, it uses months 1 to 12 alone, with nights 2026-01-01 to 2026-02-28
121	  held out from the fit. The criterion is the Recall@5 at T = 120 s of the fused ranker on those
122	  held-out training queries, ties broken by candidate recall. The alternatives are:
123	  - prefilter scaling: fixed units, dataset σ, or per-window z;
124	  - `candidate_tracks`: 200, 500 or 1,000;
125	  - training T grid: {60, 90, 120} or {45, 60, 90, 120, 180}.
126	
127	  The defaults are fixed units, 500 and {45, 60, 90, 120, 180}. Months 13 to 18 and the demo are never
128	  a selection criterion. No setting is special-cased for an incident, actor or base.
129	- **A4 · D-071 · Partial live signature (§10.5 "live signatures are partial").** The query signature is
130	  `features.signatures.signature()` run on the query's own features, its first point and its last
131	  point at or before T, plus a sensor context bounded to T. RF and Remote ID detections, the track's
132	  own points and the other tracks' spans (the concurrency test, D-048) all count only up to T. Unknown
133	  fields give 0.5 in fusion, as §10.5 says. Candidate signatures come from `TrackStore.tracks_before`
134	  (§11.3), one call per query.
135	- **A5 · D-072 · Two read-only `TrackStore` port methods.** `sensor_context_until(track_id, until) ->
136	  dict` (`rf_family`, `rid_serials`, `rid_operator_xy`) and `features_many(track_ids) -> DataFrame`.
137	  They are implemented in `DuckTrackStore` by giving the existing `rf_association` and
138	  `rid_association` SQL an optional `until` bound. It defaults to None, so phase 3's calls and tests
139	  are unchanged. This is a deviation from §4.1. Without them, `match/` would hold SQL text, or
140	  pay one round trip per candidate (fact 2). The KDB-X swap (§22) needs these two in its adapter. The
141	  matcher keeps a per-process cache of candidate features: history features never change between
142	  index builds.
143	- **A6 · D-073 · Fusion training (§10.6).**
144	  - `kairos_defense.eval.training` builds the pairs, and is the only place that reads truth for them.
145	  - Queries: history prober, copycat and swarm-drone tracks on nights before 2026-03-01 (months 1 to 12),
146	    at T ∈ {45, 60, 90, 120, 180}. The candidates are exactly what the matcher's prefilter returns:
147	    same code, `start < q.start`, own incident excluded.
148	  - Label: same `actor_id` (a swarm drone's actor is its team). Hobbyists and copycats are the
149	    negatives. Queries with no positive pair still add negatives.
150	  - τ = median `d_norm` of the positive pairs. `shape_sim` is then computed with that τ.
151	  - `LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced", solver="lbfgs", max_iter=1000, C=1.0)`, feature order
152	    from `scoring.fusion.features`, on rows sorted by (query, T, candidate) so the fit is deterministic.
153	  - Validation: the same build on months 13 to 18, recording pair counts, ROC AUC, log loss and the
154	    validation Recall@5 at T = 120 s. These are reported only and never used for selection (A3).
155	  - Artifacts:
156	    - `models/dtw_calibration.json`: `version`, `created_at`, `tau`, `n_pairs`, `n_positive`,
157	      same-actor and other `d_norm` p10 / p50 / p90, `band_fraction`, `anchor`, `training_hash`.
158	    - `models/fusion_v1.json`: `version` `fusion-v1`, `created_at`, `features`, `coefficients`,

435	
436	Run on the dev laptop from the build's working tree, after `make index`, which the new vectors
437	require. Each command is timed with `/usr/bin/time -p` or the shell's `time`, and its output trimmed
438	into `EXIT_CHECK.md`. The SPEC §20 exit check is run exactly as written. If `make eval` exits 1 (a
439	demo assertion or a regression), the `&&` chain stops, so `match` is then run on its own and both
440	outcomes are recorded.

442	```bash
443	make index
444	make models && make eval && uv run kairos-defense match --method dtw --incident DEMO-BRAVO-0828 --at 90
445	uv run kairos-defense eval --baseline
446	python3 scripts/check_targets.py 4; echo "check_targets exit $?"
447	make check && make test-all
448	```

451	|---|---|---|

459	| Live top 3 with reasons | `match --method dtw --incident DEMO-BRAVO-0828 --at 90` | Table rows 1 to 3 with incident, score, shape, warp and reasons. ALPHA-0303 should read "flown 18% slower" |
460	| Baseline written | `eval --baseline` | `reports/baseline.json` (method `dtw`) |
461	| Targets judged | `check_targets.py 4` | PASS, WARN or GAP lines and the exit code (0, or 1 for soft gaps only) |
462	| Quality floor | `make check`, `make test-all` | Ruff clean, fast count about 417, slow passed, web check passes |
463	
464	Gate dry run (the build simulates `docs/phases/gates.json` phase 4 on the committed tree):
465	`make check`, `make models`, `make eval || echo …`, `uv run kairos-defense match --method dtw
466	--incident DEMO-BRAVO-0828 --at 90`, then `python3 scripts/check_targets.py 4`. `reports/baseline.json`
467	and both model files are committed, so the gate finds them. The gate does not run `make index`: it
468	reuses the build's `data/`. The A8 guard turns a stale index into a clear failure rather than wrong
469	numbers.
470	
471	## Documentation to write or update
472	
473	- `docs/phases/phase-04/EXIT_CHECK.md` and `REPORT.md` (templates). REPORT's Metrics compare phase 3
474	  (Euclidean, per-window z), the in-run Euclidean on fixed vectors, and DTW plus fusion. It shows
475	  per-actor Recall@5, the live ranks of all five earlier P1 flights at T+90, and any A3 attempts.
476	- `src/kairos_defense/match/README.md`: the pipeline, the new modules, the API, the timings, the
477	  model files, the guards and the gotchas (`use_c=True` everywhere; warp only for the top 20; psi).
478	- `src/kairos_defense/eval/README.md`: training, `TrainSplit`, the new metric keys, the in-run lift,
479	  the demo assertion, `baseline.json`, the font pin.
480	- `src/kairos_defense/features/README.md`: `normalize`, `channel_scales`, and the fact that the index
481	  must be rebuilt.
482	- `src/kairos_defense/store/README.md`: the two new port methods and `until`.
483	- `src/kairos_defense/config/README.md`: the new keys.
484	- `src/kairos_defense/README.md`: the ports and the CLI (`models`, the method defaults).
485	- Root `README.md` "Status": phase 4 row, and the "Works today" line gains `make models`, `make eval`
486	  (DTW) and `match --method dtw`.
487	- `docs/PROGRESS.md`: a session-log entry and the one-line evidence (the Status cell is left to the
488	  autopilot).
489	- `docs/DECISIONS.md`: D-068 to D-077 as above. D-058 and D-062 are each marked resolved, by D-068 and
490	  D-064, in their new entries.
491	
492	## Risks and mitigations
493	
494	1. **The live top 3 may miss by one place.** The prototype has CHARLIE-260710 third and ALPHA-0502
495	   fourth (fact 4). Both are true P1 flights; CHARLIE is planted as weaker.
496	   - Mitigation: build the real partial signature (A4); add swarm drones and the wider T grid to
497	     training (A6); try only the A3 alternatives, judged on the training split.
498	   - The build must never special-case incidents, bases or the demo, and never edit the demo
499	     assertion or the query sets.
500	   - If it still misses, it is a soft GAP (D-063), shown in REPORT.md with the ranks and fused
501	     contributions of the five P1 flights.
502	2. **A copycat outranks a true match.** C1 copies P1's shape. The fusion's RF family, launch area and
503	   time of night must separate them: a fast test with the fixture model and a slow test on full data.
504	3. **Look-ahead through the partial signature.** RF and Remote ID heard after T, or the concurrency
505	   test using later tracks, would leak. Mitigation: everything is bounded by `until`, with a tamper
506	   test, plus the new DTW no-look-ahead test.
507	4. **Truth leakage into the matcher.** Only `eval/training.py` labels pairs. `match/` receives plain
508	   arrays and JSON files, and the §7.6 scan (`test_truth_isolation.py`) covers the new modules.
509	5. **A stale index at gate time** (the gate does not run `make index`). Mitigation: the A8 guard, and
510	   the build runs `make index` before the exit check.
511	6. **A dtaidistance API quirk** (silent pure Python, psi and `best_path` semantics). Mitigation: one
512	   adapter module (`dtw_rerank.py`), `require_c()`, `use_c=True` on every call, and known-answer tests
513	   for warps 0.8 to 1.4.
514	7. **Latency.** Bounded sensor-context SQL per query, 500 candidates and the feature cache's cold
515	   start. All of it is measured per stage and reported only (D-060). Expected end to end is well under
516	   1.5 s, from facts 1 and 2. Training builds about 200,000 pairs, in about 1 to 3 minutes.
517	8. **Fixture data cannot train a real model.** The P1 nights have few positives in months 1 to 12.
518	   Mitigation: `TrainSplit` parameters in tests and a hand-set `toy_models` fixture for matcher tests.
519	   Real training is covered by the slow tests and the exit check.
520	9. **The passing test count must not drop.** Two stub assertions are replaced, never deleted, and the
521	   `models` stub case leaves with the stub. About 50 new tests are added.
522	10. **Overfitting the time of night.** The prototype's `tod_sim` coefficient is large: probers keep
523	    schedules, hobbyists do not. That is an honest signal in this synthetic world. It is reported in
524	    REPORT.md and not suppressed.
525	11. **Module size and the 5% gate.** Splits as planned in A11. Copycat-first at 0 turns any single copycat
526	    query into a "regression" under §19.4. Accepted: the gate tolerates `make eval`'s exit code (A9).
527	
528	## Out of scope
529	
530	- Swarm matching and `swarm_top1` (phase 9). Time to match ≥ 70% (phase 9's gate; reported now).
531	- Report recall, clue extraction and the analog forecast (phase 5).
532	- `match_proposed` ledger events and model-version recording in the ledger (phase 6). The model
533	  version is already on every `Match`.
534	- Streaming, `replay --precompute` and the UI Match Explainer (phases 7 and 8);
535	  `explain_alignment` is built now for phase 8.
536	- LB_Keogh pruning (A2), and D-046's P6 and C2 target choice (not needed for the targets).
537	- Pinning the font in `sim/figures.py` (D-065): phase 4 does not change `sim/`.
538	
539	## Review changes
540	
541	None yet.

# Phase 4: DTW matcher and fusion model, plan

Autopilot plan step, 2026-10-28. Written without a human in the loop (CLAUDE.md rule 5, `phase-auto`):
every assumption below is recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` during the build.

## Goal

Build the real matcher (SPEC §10.4 to §10.8): a DTW re-rank of the prefilter's candidates, a calibrated
shape similarity, a logistic fusion of shape and context features trained on history only, warp ratio,
explanations, `make models`, and `kairos-defense match --method dtw`. Then run `make eval` with the DTW
matcher and write the first `reports/baseline.json`.

Phase 4 targets (SPEC §20, `scripts/check_targets.py 4`): Recall@5 at T = 120 s ≥ 0.80, DTW lift ≥ +0.10,
copycat-first ≤ 5%, the §10.9 latencies (report only, D-060), and the demo rows
`live_first_contact_local`, `live_orbit_established_s` and `live_top3_incidents`, all `pass`. At T+90 the
live top 3 must be P1-DELTA-260419, P1-ALPHA-260303 and P1-ALPHA-260502 (any order), each with a score
and reasons.

## Inputs read

- `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/PROGRESS.md` (phases 0 to 3 and their backfills), `docs/phases/TEMPLATES.md`,
  `docs/phases/phase-03/REPORT.md`, `docs/phases/gates.json`, `scripts/check_targets.py`.
- SPEC §1.2 (T+90 beat: "flown ~18% slower"), §6.5, §7.2, §7.5, §8.10, §9 (§9.3's normalization), §10
  (all), §19 (all), §20 phase 4.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`, in particular D-003, D-013, D-020, D-046, D-047, D-048, D-049, D-050, D-051,
  D-053 to D-060, D-062 to D-064 and D-067. Next free number: **D-068**.
- Code: `match/` (query, prefilter, baseline, types), `features/windows.py`, `features/channels.py`,
  `features/signatures.py`, `store/duck.py`, `store/lance.py`, `ports.py`, `config/scoring.py`,
  `eval/` (harness, metrics, demo, report, truth), `cli.py`, and the tests that touch them
  (`test_cli.py`, `test_eval_harness.py`, `test_no_lookahead.py`, `test_windows.py`,
  `test_truth_isolation.py`, `tests/slow/test_full_index.py`).

### Facts checked during planning (read-only; nothing in the repo or `data/` was written)

1. **The C path works on the laptop (D-062 resolved by D-064).** `dtw.try_import_c()` is True.
   `dtw_ndim.distance(L, S, window=60, use_c=True)` on 120×5 against 240×5 takes 0.064 ms.
   `dtw_ndim.warping_paths(..., use_c=True)` (or `warping_paths_fast`) plus `dtw.best_path` takes
   0.4 ms. Without `use_c` it takes 36 ms, so every call must pass `use_c=True`.
2. **LanceDB returns many candidate tracks cheaply.** For the live query at T+90 (W = 60, filtered),
   `k` = 200 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 windows gives 185 / 1,102 / 1,545 / 1,728 distinct tracks in about
   14 / 18 / 21 / 25 ms. Loading all 800,148 `track_features` rows takes 46 ms (58 MB). 50 separate
   `features()` calls take 76 ms.
3. **D-058's cause is the per-window z-normalization, and option (a) fixes most of it.** A brute-force
   rebuild of the 60 s and 120 s windows in memory with fixed per-channel scales (speed 5 m/s, turn
   10 °/s, distance 200 m, altitude 30 m, climb 1 m/s; times the §6.5 weights; then PAA and L2) instead
   of per-window z-normalization gives:

   | Same-actor track among the candidates (23 prober queries) | per-window z (phase 3) | fixed scales |
   |---|---:|---:|
   | top 50 at T = 90 s | 0.70 | 0.91 |
   | top 50 at T = 120 s | 0.74 | 0.83 |
   | top 200 at T = 120 s | 0.78 | 0.96 |
   | live T+90: ranks of DELTA, ALPHA-0303, ALPHA-0502 among 1,882 tracks | 855 / 953 / 564 | 318 / 23 / 436 |

4. **The full pipeline, prototyped, reaches the targets with a wide candidate list (D-058 (a) + (b)).**
   This was a scratch prototype: §10.4 anchored segments with per-series z-normalized banded DTW, the
   seven §10.5 features, τ = median same-actor `d_norm`, and `LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced")`
   trained on months 1 to 12 (54 prober and copycat queries at T = 60, 90, 120). It was evaluated on the
   23 month 13 to 18 prober queries.

   | Prefilter vectors, candidates | Recall@5 T=120 | top 3 T=90 | copycat-first T=120 | Euclidean Recall@5 T=120 | live T+90 ranks DELTA / ALPHA-0303 / ALPHA-0502 |
   |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
   | fixed, 50 | 0.83 | 0.91 | 0.13 | 0.43 | – / 1 / – |
   | fixed, 200 | 0.96 | 0.96 | 0.00 | 0.43 | – / 1 / – |
   | **fixed, 500** | **1.00** | **0.96** | **0.00** | **0.43** | **1 / 2 / 4** (CHARLIE 3rd) |
   | per-window z, 500 | 0.91 | 0.91 | 0.09 | 0.48 | – / – / – |
   | dataset σ (global z), 500 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.00 | 0.61 | 2 / 3 / 5 (BRAVO-251114 1st, CHARLIE 4th) |
   | fixed, 500, DTW on fixed scales too | 1.00 | 0.96 | 0.00 | 0.43 | 4 / 1 / 20 |
   | fixed, 500, extra `target_match` feature | 1.00 | 0.96 | 0.00 | 0.43 | 5 / 17 / 20 |

   With the best setting the live top 3 misses by one place: CHARLIE-260710, the planted "weaker match
   on purpose", is third, and ALPHA-0502 is fourth. Both are true P1 flights. **Disclosure:** these
   planning numbers looked at the month 13 to 18 queries and the demo. The build chooses its settings
   by the training-split rule in "Assumptions" A3, not by these tables.
5. **§10.4's warp ratio cannot work as literally written.** Aligning a W-row live matrix end to end
   with a 2W-row anchored segment forces the path slope to about 1.7 whatever the true warp: a synthetic
   flight warped by 1.0 / 1.22 / 0.95 / 0.8 gives slopes 1.67 / 1.74 / 1.65 / 1.63. Normalizing each
   series over itself also biases it, even with relaxed ends: 1.38 / 1.58 / 1.31 / 1.06. With **both**
   series normalized by the live window's μ and σ **and** psi relaxation on the segment's two ends
   (`psi = (0, 0, m − n, m − n)`, best end column of the last row, `dtw.best_path(paths, row=n, col=j)`),
   the slopes are 1.002 / 1.221 / 0.95 / 0.80 / 1.40 for W = 60 and W = 120. A warp of 1.22 then gives
   "18% slower", which is the §1.2 beat.

## Assumptions and decisions

Each one becomes a `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry during the build (numbers are provisional).

- **A1 · D-068 · D-058 resolved: fixed-unit window vectors plus a wide candidate list.**
  - `features.channel_scales: [5.0, 10.0, 200.0, 30.0, 1.0]` (m/s, °/s, m, m, m/s) and
    `windows.normalize: fixed` are new keys in `config/scoring.yaml`. `fixed` means
    `raw / scale × weight`, with no centering, the D-051 NaN interpolation, then PAA and L2. `window`
    keeps phase 3's per-window z-normalization (§9.3 as written) for comparison and for the phase 3
    unit tests.
  - `prefilter.k_windows: 10000` and `prefilter.candidate_tracks: 500`.
  - This deviates from §9.3 (normalization "over the series being compared") for the prefilter vectors
    only; DTW keeps §9.3 (A2). It also deviates from §6.5's 200 / 50.
  - Why: fact 3 and fact 4. Per-window z-normalization erases the orbit radius, the speeds and the
    altitude that make P1 distinctive. The DTW plus fusion cost of 500 candidates is about 30 ms.
  - `make index` must be rerun. A self-check refuses a stale index (A8).
- **A2 · D-069 · DTW details (§10.4).**
  - Shape distance as written: anchored segment `[o − 0.5W, o + 1.5W]` clipped to the track; each series
    z-normalized over itself and weighted (§9.3); NaN interpolated, an all-NaN channel set to 0;
    `dtw_ndim.distance(L, S, window=int(0.25 × max(n, m)), use_c=True)`;
    `d_norm = d / sqrt(n)`; `shape_sim = exp(−d_norm / τ)`.
  - The C path is mandatory (D-013, D-020): `require_c()` raises `DtwUnavailable` when
    `dtw.try_import_c()` is False. Every call passes `use_c=True`.
  - Warp ratio (fact 5): a second alignment with L and S both scaled by L's μ and σ (weighted), psi
    relaxation `(0, 0, m − n, m − n)` when `m > n` (none otherwise), and the same band. Take the best
    end column of the last row, then `dtw.best_path`. `k` is the least-squares slope of segment index
    against live index. It is computed for the top `EXPLAIN_TOP = 20` fused matches only (the ones shown
    and explained); the others keep `warp_ratio = NaN` (no invented numbers, D-054).
  - Text (§10.4 step 5): `k > 1.1` → "flown X% slower" with X = round((1 − 1/k) × 100); `k < 0.9` →
    "flown X% faster" with X = round((1/k − 1) × 100). §10.4 gives only the slower formula; the faster one
    is its mirror.
  - Step 6: `explain_alignment()` wraps `subsequence_alignment` on the `dist_target_m` channel and is
    tested now. The phase 8 Match Explainer will call it.
  - The optional LB_Keogh pruning is not built: 500 DTW calls take about 30 ms, and `lb_keogh` needs
    equal lengths while L and S differ.
- **A3 · D-070 · Settings are chosen on the training split only.** If the build needs to choose among
  pre-registered alternatives, it uses months 1 to 12 alone, with nights 2026-01-01 to 2026-02-28
  held out from the fit. The criterion is the Recall@5 at T = 120 s of the fused ranker on those
  held-out training queries, ties broken by candidate recall. The alternatives are:
  - prefilter scaling: fixed units, dataset σ, or per-window z;
  - `candidate_tracks`: 200, 500 or 1,000;
  - training T grid: {60, 90, 120} or {45, 60, 90, 120, 180}.

  The defaults are fixed units, 500 and {45, 60, 90, 120, 180}. Months 13 to 18 and the demo are never
  a selection criterion. No setting is special-cased for an incident, actor or base.
- **A4 · D-071 · Partial live signature (§10.5 "live signatures are partial").** The query signature is
  `features.signatures.signature()` run on the query's own features, its first point and its last
  point at or before T, plus a sensor context bounded to T. RF and Remote ID detections, the track's
  own points and the other tracks' spans (the concurrency test, D-048) all count only up to T. Unknown
  fields give 0.5 in fusion, as §10.5 says. Candidate signatures come from `TrackStore.tracks_before`
  (§11.3), one call per query.
- **A5 · D-072 · Two read-only `TrackStore` port methods.** `sensor_context_until(track_id, until) ->
  dict` (`rf_family`, `rid_serials`, `rid_operator_xy`) and `features_many(track_ids) -> DataFrame`.
  They are implemented in `DuckTrackStore` by giving the existing `rf_association` and
  `rid_association` SQL an optional `until` bound. It defaults to None, so phase 3's calls and tests
  are unchanged. This is a deviation from §4.1. Without them, `match/` would hold SQL text, or
  pay one round trip per candidate (fact 2). The KDB-X swap (§22) needs these two in its adapter. The
  matcher keeps a per-process cache of candidate features: history features never change between
  index builds.
- **A6 · D-073 · Fusion training (§10.6).**
  - `kairos_defense.eval.training` builds the pairs, and is the only place that reads truth for them.
  - Queries: history prober, copycat and swarm-drone tracks on nights before 2026-03-01 (months 1 to 12),
    at T ∈ {45, 60, 90, 120, 180}. The candidates are exactly what the matcher's prefilter returns:
    same code, `start < q.start`, own incident excluded.
  - Label: same `actor_id` (a swarm drone's actor is its team). Hobbyists and copycats are the
    negatives. Queries with no positive pair still add negatives.
  - τ = median `d_norm` of the positive pairs. `shape_sim` is then computed with that τ.
  - `LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced", solver="lbfgs", max_iter=1000, C=1.0)`, feature order
    from `scoring.fusion.features`, on rows sorted by (query, T, candidate) so the fit is deterministic.
  - Validation: the same build on months 13 to 18, recording pair counts, ROC AUC, log loss and the
    validation Recall@5 at T = 120 s. These are reported only and never used for selection (A3).
  - Artifacts:
    - `models/dtw_calibration.json`: `version`, `created_at`, `tau`, `n_pairs`, `n_positive`,
      same-actor and other `d_norm` p10 / p50 / p90, `band_fraction`, `anchor`, `training_hash`.
    - `models/fusion_v1.json`: `version` `fusion-v1`, `created_at`, `features`, `coefficients`,
      `intercept`, `tau`, `training_hash`, `train_split`, `validation`.
    - `training_hash` is SHA-256 over the sorted pair keys, X and y. It is deterministic;
      `created_at` is the only field that changes.
  - A numeric `scoring.dtw.tau` overrides the calibration. `auto` reads `dtw_calibration.json`.
  - The split dates are parameters (`TrainSplit`) with the §10.6 defaults, so unit tests can train
    on the P1 nights.
- **A7 · D-074 · Explanations (§10.7).**
  - Contribution = `coef_i × x_i`. Reasons are the features whose §10.7 condition holds, ordered by
    contribution, at most three.
  - The warp reason ("Same shape, flown 18% slower") ranks with `shape_sim`'s contribution and needs a
    warp ratio outside 0.9 to 1.1.
  - Values in the text are the past flight's signature values: family, bearing rounded to 5°, radius
    rounded to 10 m.
- **A8 · D-075 · Stale-index and missing-model guards.** `models`, `eval --method dtw` and `match
  --method dtw` rebuild one stored window's vector from `features_many` with the current config and
  search for it with `window_id = '<id>'`, k = 1. A `_distance` above 1e-6 means the index was built
  with another vector recipe, so they stop with "index is stale: run make index". Without
  `models/fusion_v1.json`, `eval` and `match --method dtw` stop with "no fusion model: run make models".
  All of these exit 1.
- **A9 · D-076 · Evaluation (§19).**
  - `eval` and `match` default to `--method dtw`. `--method euclidean` still runs (§10.2).
  - **DTW lift is measured in the same run, on the same index and queries:** the Euclidean ranks are
    the prefilter order of the same candidates, which is the §10.2 baseline. New `Outcome` fields:
    `baseline_rank`, `baseline_copycat_rank` and `dtw_ms`.
  - New metric keys: `recall_at_5_t120_baseline`, `dtw_lift`, `latency_dtw_p50_ms`,
    `latency_dtw_p95_ms` (all candidates, 500, not §10.9's 50: the harder case) and
    `candidate_tracks`. The REPORT also states the lift over phase 3's frozen 0.435.
  - `dtw_lift` and `latency_dtw_p95_ms` join `GATED` and leave `PENDING`.
  - The demo row `live_top3_incidents` becomes an assertion: `pass` when all three expected incidents
    are in the top 3 and each has a score and at least one reason, else `fail`.
  - D-056's question: the §19.4 5% rule stays as written, with no absolute floor. `gates.json`
    tolerates a non-zero `make eval`, and `check_targets.py` judges the targets.
  - The JSON's `method` is `dtw`. Its title reads "DTW + fusion".
- **A10 · D-077 · Font pinned in `eval/report.py`** (the D-065 and D-067 follow-up, since this phase
  edits the file): `plt.rc_context({"font.family": "DejaVu Sans"})` around the figure, so the figure is
  the same on every machine. `sim/figures.py` is not touched (phase 4 does not change `sim/`).
- **A11 · Module size.** If `eval/report.py` (286 lines) or `cli.py` (307 lines) would go past about 400
  lines, the Markdown writer moves to `eval/report_md.py` and the match and models table printers move to
  `cli_tables.py`.

## Work breakdown

Each step ends with `make check` green.

1. **Config and vectors (D-068).**
   - `src/kairos_defense/config/scoring.py`: `FeaturesConfig.channel_scales: list[Pos]`, one per
     channel (validated); `WindowsConfig.normalize: Literal["window", "fixed"]`.
   - `config/scoring.yaml`: `channel_scales`, `normalize: fixed`, `k_windows: 10000`,
     `candidate_tracks: 500`, with comments citing D-068.
   - `src/kairos_defense/features/windows.py`: `window_vectors(..., scales=None)` (None means per-window
     z, phase 3 behavior); `iter_windows` and `query_vector` pass the scales when `normalize == "fixed"`.
     The function is still shared by the index and the query (D-051).
   - Tests: `test_config.py` invalid variants, and the new `test_windows.py` tests.
   - Then run `make index`. The window counts must equal phase 3's (57,462 / 51,297 / 27,507).
2. **Ports and adapter (D-071, D-072).**
   - `src/kairos_defense/ports.py`: `TrackStore.sensor_context_until(track_id, until)` and
     `features_many(track_ids)`.
   - `src/kairos_defense/store/duck.py`: `rf_association` and `rid_association` take an optional
     `until`. It bounds the points and the detections to `ts ≤ until`, and the concurrency spans to
     tracks whose first point is at or before `until`, with their points clipped to `until`. Add
     `sensor_context_until(track_id, until)` (one track) and `features_many`. The bulk
     `sensor_context(track_ids=None)`, used by `index` and by phase 3's tests, keeps its name and
     behavior (adapter-only, D-053).
   - Tests: `test_duck_store.py` additions.
3. **DTW re-rank (D-069).** `src/kairos_defense/match/dtw_rerank.py` (about 200 lines):
   - `require_c()` and `DtwUnavailable`;
   - `anchor_bounds(offset_s, W, n_rows, before, after) -> (lo, hi)`;
   - `prepare(raw, weights) -> (n, 5)`: §9.3 normalization plus NaN fill;
   - `shape_distance(L_raw, S_raw, scoring) -> d_norm`;
   - `shape_sim(d_norm, tau)`;
   - `warp_ratio(L_raw, S_raw, scoring) -> float`;
   - `warp_text(k) -> str | None`;
   - `explain_alignment(live_dist, full_dist) -> (start, end, value)`.

   These are pure functions over numpy arrays, and the only `dtaidistance` import in the package.
   Tests: `test_dtw_rerank.py`.
4. **Partial signature and fusion features (D-071).**
   - `src/kairos_defense/match/live_signature.py`: `query_signature(store, q) -> dict`, from points up
     to T and `store.sensor_context_until(track_id, until=q.start_ts + T)`.
   - `src/kairos_defense/match/fusion.py`:
     - `fusion_features(qsig, csig, shape_sim) -> dict[str, float]` (§10.5 formulas, 0.5 for unknowns);
     - `feature_matrix(rows, order) -> (n, 7) float64`;
     - frozen `FusionModel` with `predict(X) -> (n,)` (sigmoid of `X @ coef + b`), `contributions(x)`,
       `to_json()`, `load(path, expected_features)` and `save(path)`;
     - frozen `DtwCalibration` with `load` and `save`.
